title: Daily Devotional #5
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #5
Dear God,

As I sit down to read and reflect on Matthew Chapter 5, I am struck by the powerful teachings that Jesus shared with his disciples and the crowds that gathered around him. The Beatitudes, in particular, stand out to me as a powerful reminder of what it means to live a life that is pleasing to you.

The first Beatitude, "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven," reminds me that humility is at the heart of true spirituality. When I am able to recognize my own limitations and weaknesses, I am better able to rely on you and your strength. Help me to cultivate a spirit of humility in all that I do.

The second Beatitude, "Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted," reminds me that even in the midst of sorrow and pain, you are always present to comfort and console us. Help me to trust in your goodness even in the midst of difficult circumstances.

The third Beatitude, "Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth," reminds me that true strength comes not from exerting power over others, but from being gentle and humble. Help me to follow your example of meekness and humility, even in situations where I am tempted to assert my own will.

The fourth Beatitude, "Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled," reminds me that you are the source of all true goodness and righteousness. Help me to seek after you with all my heart, and to trust in your power to transform my life.

The fifth Beatitude, "Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy," reminds me that forgiveness and compassion are at the heart of your character. Help me to extend grace and mercy to those around me, even when it is difficult.

The sixth Beatitude, "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God," reminds me that holiness and purity are the foundation of a life that is pleasing to you. Help me to cultivate a pure heart, and to seek after you with sincerity and devotion.

The seventh Beatitude, "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God," reminds me that you are the God of peace, and that you call us to be agents of reconciliation and healing in the world. Help me to be a peacemaker in all my relationships, and to work for the good of others in all that I do.

Finally, the teachings in Matthew Chapter 5 remind me that following you is not always easy or comfortable. But even when the road is difficult, you are always with me, giving me strength and guidance. Help me to trust in you more fully, and to follow you with courage and faith.

In Jesus' name,
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional Day #2
paragraphs: Daily Devotional Day  #2

Matthew chapter 2 begins with the story of the wise men who came from the east to worship Jesus. As I read this chapter, I am struck by the various responses of people to the news of the Messiah's birth.

The wise men responded with joy and a deep desire to worship Jesus. They traveled a great distance and endured much hardship to pay homage to the King of kings. Their response challenges me to examine my own heart and ask myself if I am willing to go to great lengths to worship and honor Jesus. Am I willing to make sacrifices for His sake, to give up my own comfort and convenience to seek His face?

King Herod, on the other hand, responded to the news of the Messiah's birth with fear and jealousy. He saw Jesus as a threat to his own power and sought to eliminate Him. Herod's response serves as a warning to me of the dangers of pride and self-centeredness. When I focus on my own desires and ambitions, I am more likely to see Jesus as a threat to my own plans rather than the source of true life and fulfillment.

The religious leaders of the day also responded to the news of the Messiah's birth with indifference. They knew the prophecies about the coming Messiah, but they were too busy with their own religious rituals and traditions to recognize Him when He came. This reminds me of the danger of becoming so caught up in my own religious practices that I miss the true meaning and purpose of my faith. Am I too focused on outward appearances and religious rituals, or am I truly seeking to know and follow Jesus?

Finally, Joseph and Mary responded to the news of the Messiah's birth with obedience and trust in God's plan. They were willing to endure hardship and uncertainty to protect and care for their son, knowing that He was the fulfillment of God's promise to His people. Their example challenges me to trust in God's plan for my life, even when it doesn't make sense and requires me to step out in faith.

As I reflect on Matthew chapter 2, I am reminded that the way I respond to Jesus and His message has eternal consequences. Will I choose to worship Him with my whole heart, or will I allow fear, pride, or indifference to keep me from experiencing the abundant life He offers? May I follow the example of the wise men and Joseph and Mary, seeking Jesus with all my heart and trusting in His plan for my life.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #3
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #3

Matthew chapter 3 begins with the appearance of John the Baptist, who was sent by God to prepare the way for Jesus. John was a prophet and he preached a message of repentance to the people, telling them to turn away from their sins and prepare their hearts for the coming of the Messiah.

As I read through this chapter, I am struck by the humility of John the Baptist. Despite his significant role in preparing the way for Jesus, he never claimed to be anything more than a voice in the wilderness. He recognized that his mission was to point people to Jesus and to prepare the way for Him.

In verse 11, John says, "I baptize you with water for repentance. But after me comes one who is more powerful than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire." This verse reminds me that as Christians, we are not called to draw attention to ourselves or to our own accomplishments, but rather to point people to Jesus and to give Him all the glory.

Another thing that stands out to me in this chapter is the baptism of Jesus. John hesitates to baptize Jesus, recognizing that Jesus is the Son of God and therefore does not need to repent of any sins. But Jesus insists, saying that it is necessary to fulfill all righteousness.

As I reflect on this passage, I am reminded of the importance of obedience. Jesus knew that His baptism was part of God's plan for Him, even though it may not have made sense to others at the time. Sometimes God calls us to do things that may not make sense to us or to those around us, but we must trust that His ways are higher than our ways and that He has a purpose for everything.

In conclusion, Matthew chapter 3 is a powerful reminder of the humility, obedience, and faithfulness that we are called to as followers of Christ. Like John the Baptist, we are called to point people to Jesus and to prepare the way for Him. And like Jesus, we must be obedient to God's will, even when it may not make sense to us at the time. May we strive to live our lives in a way that brings glory to God and points others to His love and grace.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #4
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #4
Dear God,

As I read through Matthew Chapter 4, I am reminded of the temptations that Jesus faced while He was here on earth. Satan tried to lure Jesus away from His mission and purpose, but Jesus was steadfast in His faith and trust in You.

The first temptation that Satan presented to Jesus was to turn stones into bread. Satan wanted to tempt Jesus to use His divine power for His own personal gain. But Jesus knew that His mission was not to satisfy His own hunger but to fulfill the will of God. Jesus responded to Satan with the words, "Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God." (Matthew 4:4).

The second temptation that Satan presented to Jesus was to throw Himself down from the pinnacle of the temple, so that the angels would rescue Him. Satan wanted to tempt Jesus to test God's protection and power. But again, Jesus knew that His mission was not to put God to the test but to trust in His goodness and sovereignty. Jesus responded to Satan with the words, "You shall not put the Lord your God to the test." (Matthew 4:7).

The third temptation that Satan presented to Jesus was to worship him in exchange for all the kingdoms of the world. Satan wanted to tempt Jesus to abandon His mission and purpose in exchange for temporary power and glory. But Jesus knew that His mission was not to seek earthly power and glory but to serve and worship God alone. Jesus responded to Satan with the words, "Be gone, Satan! For it is written, 'You shall worship the Lord your God and him only shall you serve.'" (Matthew 4:10).

As I reflect on these temptations, I am reminded of the importance of staying focused on Your will and purpose for my life. The world may offer temporary pleasures and satisfaction, but true fulfillment and joy can only be found in You. Help me to trust in Your goodness and sovereignty, and to resist the temptations of the evil one. May my life be a reflection of Your love and grace, and may I seek to serve and worship You alone.

In Jesus' name,
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devo #1
paragraphs: Daily Devo #1
Dear Lord,

As I read through Matthew chapter 1, I am reminded of the rich heritage that surrounds Your coming to earth as a human being. This chapter is often overlooked as a mere list of names, but upon closer examination, it reveals the depth of Your love for us.

Firstly, I am struck by the inclusion of women in Your genealogy. In a time and culture where women were often marginalized and overlooked, You made sure to include them in Your family line. Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and Bathsheba all had difficult pasts and yet they are mentioned alongside the great patriarchs of the faith. It is a beautiful reminder that You came for all of us, regardless of our past or our present circumstances.

Secondly, I am in awe of the fact that You were born into a family line that included both kings and commoners. You didn't come only for the elite or the privileged, but for all people, no matter their social status. Your love transcends all human distinctions.

Thirdly, I am struck by the significance of Your name, "Immanuel," which means "God with us." You didn't come as a distant God, but as a human being, fully present and engaged in the lives of those around You. You walked among us, ate with us, laughed with us, and suffered with us. You understand our joys and our sorrows, our triumphs and our failures, because You have experienced them firsthand.

Finally, I am humbled by the fact that You came to save us from our sins. You didn't come to condemn us or to judge us, but to offer us forgiveness and grace. You willingly took on our sins and our shame, so that we could be reconciled to You and to one another.

Lord, as I reflect on Matthew chapter 1, I am reminded of Your great love for us. You came to us, not as a distant and unapproachable God, but as a Savior who understands our humanity and our struggles. Help me to remember this truth as I go about my day-to-day life, and to share Your love with those around me.

In Jesus' name,
Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Daily Devotional #6
paragraphs: Daily Devotional #6
Dear Heavenly Father,
As I read through Matthew chapter 6, I am reminded of the importance of seeking You above all else. In this chapter, You teach us about prayer, giving to others, and storing up treasures in heaven.

Firstly, You teach us about prayer. You remind us that we should pray in secret, not to be seen by others, but to communicate with You intimately. You also remind us not to use empty phrases or repetition, but to pray with sincerity and purpose. Help me to remember these things as I come before You in prayer, seeking Your will for my life and the needs of those around me.

You also teach us about giving to others. You remind us that we should give generously and cheerfully, not for the praise of others, but to bless those in need. You promise that when we give, we will be rewarded in heaven. Help me to have a generous heart and to seek out opportunities to give to others, even when it may not be convenient or easy.

Lastly, You teach us about storing up treasures in heaven. You remind us that our earthly possessions are temporary and can be easily destroyed, but the treasures we store up in heaven are eternal. Help me to remember this truth and to focus my heart and mind on eternal things, rather than temporary pleasures.

Lord, as I reflect on these teachings, I pray that You would help me to live them out in my daily life. May I seek You above all else, give generously to others, and store up treasures in heaven. Thank You for Your love and grace, and for the guidance You give us through Your Word.
In Jesus' name, Amen.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: You may not like the song choices on Sunday,
paragraphs:
You may not like the song choices on Sunday,
Don't worry, they weren't singing about you.
You may not like loudness or style of the music,
Don't worry, it wasn't catered for your ears.
You may not like the decor of your church,
Don't worry, your eyes should be on Him.
You may not like the one person who brought a tambourine, and it playing off beat.
Don't worry, they're definitely not playing for you.
You may not like the Pastor's message this week,
Don't worry, the person in front of you needed it.
You may not like how other people get the stage instead of you,
Don't worry, He still sees you.
You may not like the dancers dancing free,
Don't worry,
There is freedom for you too.
May our expectations never extinguish another’s celebration.
There is room for freedom in worship.
Yours may not look like theirs.
And that's okay.
God is so much bigger than one style of praise.
He dances with the dancers,
He sings with the singers,
He shouts with the shouters,
And He is still with the thinkers.
He is big enough to love them all.
There is a greater degree of joy in worship when we take off the burden of needing to like it.
It was never for us,
But it will take all of us.
May we only do what we see our Father do.
Whatever that may look like,
May it be with our everything
Manimba na kita mga igsoon! :)
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)
